title: "Fedora’s Koji Build System"

# Fedora’s Koji Build System

In the RPM ecosystem, Fedora and Red Hat Enterprise Linux rely on **Koji**—a distributed, declarative build system designed for high concurrency, cryptographic traceability, and multi-architecture targets.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                   Fedora Koji Architecture                |
|                                                           |
| 1. Developer CLI / Web UI: `fedpkg build` / `koji build`  |
|                         |                                 |
|                         v                                 |
| 2. Koji Hub (XML-RPC API daemon + PostgreSQL database)    |
|    - Authenticates maintainers via Kerberos / SSL certs   |
|    - Manages tags, targets, inheritance trees, and tasks  |
|                         |                                 |
|                         v                                 |
| 3. Koji Builders (kojid daemon running on bare metal)     |
|    - Launches `mock` inside isolated chroot               |
|    - Installs minimal buildroot based on target tag       |
|    - Executes `rpmbuild -ba package.spec`                 |
|                         |                                 |
|                         v                                 |
| 4. Tagging & Inheritance System                           |
|    - Tag: `f40-build` -> `f40-updates-candidate` -> `f40` |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Tag-Based Inheritance and Promotion

The hallmark of Koji is its **tag inheritance model**:
- Every release has a build tag (e.g., `f40-build`) that specifies exactly which RPM repository packages are visible to the compiler inside the `mock` chroot.
- When a package finishes building successfully, it is tagged as `f40-updates-candidate`.
- After passing automated openQA integration testing and receiving community karma in Fedora's Bodhi updates system, an administrator simply moves the tag pointer to `f40-updates`.
- The repository generation tool (`createrepo_c`) regenerates metadata dynamically based on the current tags in PostgreSQL.

## `mock`: Hermetic RPM Building

At the worker layer, Koji invokes **`mock`**:
- Creates an isolated chroot using Linux mount namespaces.
- Uses `dnf` to download and unpack a fresh RPM buildroot for each individual build.
- Ensures zero contamination between builds on the same physical server.
